fill_pdf.title: Fill a PDF template
fill_pdf.description: Fill a PDF template with data and get the finished PDF back as binary bytes. The template must already exist in Anvil (uploaded through the UI, which is where its field names are detected) and is addressed by its template eid. Keys in `data` are those field names -- an unknown key is ignored rather than erroring, so check the output if a field comes back blank.

pdf_template_eid.description: The PDF template's eid, from its URL in the Anvil UI.

data.description: Field values keyed by the template's field names.

version_number.description: Which published version to fill. Pass -1 to fill the unpublished draft, which is how to test template changes before publishing.

title.description: Title encoded into the PDF document metadata.

text_color.description: Default text colour as a hex code.

alignment.description: Default horizontal alignment for filled text.

font_weight.description: Default font weight for filled text.

use_interactive_fields.description: Keep the filled fields editable in the output PDF instead of flattening them.

default_read_only.description: When interactive fields are on, mark them read-only by default.

output.description: The filled PDF as binary bytes, not JSON.

generate_pdf.title: Generate a PDF from HTML or Markdown
generate_pdf.description: Build a new PDF from your own content -- no template needed. With `type: "html"`, `data` is {"html": "...", "css": "..."}; with the default `type: "markdown"`, `data` is an array of blocks each carrying a heading, a label and content, or a table. Returns raw PDF bytes. The styling arguments below apply to markdown only and are ignored for HTML, where your CSS governs.

data.description: For HTML, {"html": "...", "css": "..."}. For markdown, the array of content blocks.

title.description: Title encoded into the PDF document metadata.

page.description: Page setup -- width, height, margins and pageCount.

font_size.description: Font size in points. Markdown only.

text_color.description: Text colour as a hex code. Markdown only.

include_timestamp.description: Show the generated-at timestamp in the footer. Markdown only; on by default.

logo.description: Logo for the document header -- {"src", "maxWidth", "maxHeight"}. Markdown only.

output.description: The generated PDF as binary bytes, not JSON.

get_current_user.title: Get the API user and their objects
get_current_user.description: The account behind the API key, with the organizations it can reach and each organization's Etch packets, PDF templates (casts), workflows (welds) and webforms (forges). The cheapest way to confirm the credential works and to discover the eids every other tool takes.

output.description: The API user and the organizations, templates, workflows and webforms it can see.

get_organization.title: Get an organization
get_organization.description: One organization by slug or eid, with its templates, workflows and webforms. Use it when an account spans several organizations and you need the eids for a specific one rather than all of them.

organization_slug.description: The organization's slug. Pass this or organization_eid.

organization_eid.description: The organization's eid. Pass this or organization_slug.

output.description: The organization and its objects.

create_etch_packet.title: Create an e-signature packet
create_etch_packet.description: Create an Etch packet -- one or more documents plus the signers who must sign them, in order. `files` references PDF templates by castEid or supplies files inline; `signers` lists each signer with the fields they sign. With `is_draft` true nothing is sent and the packet waits for send_etch_packet; with it false the first signer is emailed immediately. Use `is_test` to exercise the flow with a watermarked packet.

name.description: A name for the packet, shown in the Anvil UI and in signer emails.

files.description: The documents in the packet -- each references a PDF template by castEid, or supplies a file inline with its fields.

signers.description: The signers in signing order, each with id, name, email, signerType and the fields they sign.

data.description: Fill data for the packet's templates, keyed by payload id.

is_draft.description: Create the packet without sending it. False emails the first signer straight away.

is_test.description: Create a watermarked test packet instead of a billable one.

signature_email_subject.description: Subject line for the signature request email.

signature_email_body.description: Body text for the signature request email.

signature_page_options.description: Customises the signing page's text and colours.

webhook_url.description: A webhook url for this packet's events specifically, overriding the organization's.

reply_to_name.description: Reply-to name on the signature emails.

reply_to_email.description: Reply-to address on the signature emails.

merge_pdfs.description: Merge all the packet's files into one PDF before signing.

allow_updates.description: Allow the packet's data and signers to be updated after creation, which is what progressive signing needs.

output.description: The created packet with its eid, status and signers.

get_etch_packet.title: Get an e-signature packet
get_etch_packet.description: Fetch one Etch packet by eid, with its status, its document group and every signer's current signing status. This is how to poll whether a packet has been completed rather than waiting on webhooks.

output.description: The packet, its documents and its signers.

send_etch_packet.title: Send an e-signature packet
send_etch_packet.description: Send a draft packet to its first signer, or resend the request to whichever signer it is currently waiting on. This is the call that actually puts a document in front of a person, so it is not reversible by another API call -- the signer receives the email.

output.description: The packet as it stands after sending.

update_etch_packet.title: Update a packet's data between signers
update_etch_packet.description: Change the fill data on an in-flight packet -- what progressive signing needs when a later signer's document depends on an earlier one's answers. By default `payload` replaces the stored data; `merge_payloads` merges it instead. The packet must have been created with allowUpdates.

payload.description: The updated fill data for the packet's documents.

merge_payloads.description: Merge into the existing data instead of replacing it.

output.description: The packet after the update.

generate_etch_sign_url.title: Get an embedded signing URL for a signer
generate_etch_sign_url.description: Mint a signing url for one signer so they can sign inside your own app instead of following an email link. The url carries an embedded token and expires in about two hours, so generate it at the moment the person is ready to sign rather than storing it. `client_user_id` is your own id for that person, recorded for traceability.

signer_eid.description: The signer's eid, from the packet's signers list.

client_user_id.description: Your own identifier for the person signing, recorded on the signature.

output.description: The short-lived embedded signing url.

get_signer.title: Get a signer
get_signer.description: One signer by eid, with their name, email, routing order and current status. Narrower than fetching the whole packet when you only need to know whether one person has signed.

output.description: The signer's details and status.

update_signer.title: Update a signer
update_signer.description: Correct a signer's name or email on an in-flight packet -- the usual fix for a typo'd address that bounced -- or activate a pending signer so the packet moves on to them. Changing the email re-sends the request to the new address.

email.description: The signer's corrected email address. Changing it re-sends the request there.

activate_if_pending.description: Activate the signer if they are still pending, moving the packet on to them.

output.description: The signer after the update.

expire_signer_tokens.title: Expire a signer's access tokens
expire_signer_tokens.description: Invalidate every signing link and embedded token issued to one signer. Use it when a signing url may have gone to the wrong person -- it does not cancel the packet, only the access, so a fresh url can be minted afterwards.

signer_eid.description: The signer whose tokens should be invalidated.

output.description: The signer after their tokens were expired.

remove_etch_packet.title: Delete an e-signature packet
remove_etch_packet.description: Delete an Etch packet outright. Irreversible, and it takes the packet's documents and signature records with it -- for an in-flight packet that simply should not proceed, expiring the signer's tokens is usually the safer move.

output.description: Confirmation that the packet was removed.

get_cast.title: Get a PDF template
get_cast.description: One PDF template (a "cast" in Anvil's vocabulary) by eid, with its field definitions. Those field names are exactly the keys `fill_pdf` expects, so this is the way to discover them rather than guessing from the document.

version_number.description: Which version to read. Pass -1 for the unpublished draft.

output.description: The template and its field configuration.

get_weld.title: Get a workflow
get_weld.description: One workflow (a "weld") by eid or slug, with the webforms and documents it strings together. Read this to learn a workflow's structure before starting or inspecting submissions against it.

eid.description: The workflow's eid. Pass this or slug.

slug.description: The workflow's slug, which needs organization_slug alongside it.

organization_slug.description: The organization the slug belongs to.

version_number.description: Which version to read. Pass -1 for the unpublished draft.

output.description: The workflow and its webforms.

get_weld_data.title: Get a workflow submission
get_weld_data.description: One submission through a workflow, with the data captured at each step and the documents it produced. This is the record to read when asking "what did this applicant actually submit, and where did it get to".

output.description: The submission, its per-step payloads and its documents.

get_forge.title: Get a webform
get_forge.description: One webform (a "forge") by eid or slug, with its field configuration. Those field names are what a submission's payload is keyed on, so read this before writing to or interpreting a submission.

eid.description: The webform's eid. Pass this or eid_or_slug.

eid_or_slug.description: The webform's eid or slug, with organization_slug alongside for a slug.

organization_slug.description: The organization the slug belongs to.

version_number.description: Which version to read. Pass -1 for the unpublished draft.

output.description: The webform and its field configuration.

create_webhook.title: Create a webhook
create_webhook.description: Register a url to receive Anvil's event callbacks for an organization. Which events actually fire is controlled by webhook actions configured separately, so a freshly created webhook may be silent until those are added in the UI.

url.description: The https endpoint Anvil should POST events to.

organization_eid.description: The organization the webhook belongs to.

output.description: The created webhook.

remove_webhook.title: Delete a webhook
remove_webhook.description: Remove a webhook endpoint. Events that would have gone to it are not queued or replayed afterwards, so anything that happens while it is gone is simply not delivered.

output.description: Confirmation that the webhook was removed.

run_graphql_query.title: Run any Anvil GraphQL query or mutation
run_graphql_query.description: Send an arbitrary query or mutation to Anvil's GraphQL endpoint, for the parts of the schema no named tool above covers -- duplicating casts, publishing welds, submitting forges, managing organization users and so on. You must know the schema; nothing here validates the document. Prefer a named tool wherever one exists, and remember a mutation sent this way can create or destroy real documents.

operation_name.description: Which operation to run, when the document defines several.

output.description: Anvil's GraphQL response -- `data` for the result, `errors` when the document failed.
